title: LUNAR Lab awarded NSF grant for cognitive NLP research
description:
We are pleased to announce that the LUNAR Lab has been awarded a three-year grant from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support our research on the cognitive plausibility of neural language model representations.

The project, titled "Meaning in Minds and Machines: Aligning Neural Language Representations with Human Semantic Memory," will investigate the degree to which the internal representations of large language models reflect the conceptual structures observed in human cognition. Using a combination of behavioral experiments, neuroimaging data, and representational similarity analysis, we aim to develop a principled framework for evaluating alignment between human and model semantics.

This funding will support two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher over the grant period, and will enable us to run large-scale human participant studies in partnership with the Brown Cognitive Linguistics and Psycholinguistics groups.

The broader impact of this work includes developing better evaluation protocols for language models, informing the design of more cognitively grounded training objectives, and contributing to the scientific understanding of how meaning is structured in both biological and artificial systems.

We are grateful to NSF for recognizing the importance of this research direction and look forward to sharing results as the project develops.
